reading.body:
Six AI governance postings, from six different employers, and only one names compute or infrastructure in its title.

The pattern is dispersion rather than team building. No employer appears twice, so these read as six separate bets on a role type rather than one company staffing a function. The titles split in two directions. Cohere and Anthropic hire for external policy and regulatory work, with Cohere's remit naming compute, infrastructure and sovereign AI. Databricks, Kong and ServiceNow attach governance to product marketing or cloud financial operations. Locations are Munich, London, San Francisco, New York and Santa Clara, with the Cohere role listed as remote in the United States.

For AI scaling, the notable thing is how little of this hiring touches the physical stack. Compute, infrastructure and power appear in exactly one title, and that role is a public policy position rather than an engineering or operations one. If power and buildings are the binding constraint, this sample shows governance hiring organized around regulation and product positioning instead. Six postings cannot establish that as a market fact, only as a reading of what was open on one day.

What the data does not cover is volume, pay, seniority or trend. The Databricks posting is dated April 2026 while the other five fall between late June and mid September, so the set spans five months rather than a single hiring moment. No federal postings appear, despite USAJobs being among the sources drawn on.
